title: Folic Acid Tablets 5mg: summary of product characteristics
authors: Ennogen Pharma Limited; Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
journal: MHRA Products, summary of product characteristics, PL 40147/0037, text revised 2 June 2025
funder: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
result: Contraindications: not to be given alone in Addisonian anaemia or other vitamin B12 deficiency states because it may precipitate subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord; long-term folate therapy is contraindicated in untreated cobalamin deficiency, including lifelong vegetarians; in elderly people a cobalamin absorption test should precede long-term therapy; folate given to such patients for 3 months or longer has precipitated cobalamin neuropathy; not for use in malignant disease unless megaloblastic anaemia from folate deficiency is an important complication. Warnings: folic acid can mask B12 deficiency while subacute irreversible damage to the nervous system continues; folate should not be routinely used in patients receiving coronary stents; caution in patients who may have folate-dependent tumours; the 5 mg tablet is not intended for healthy pregnant women, for whom lower doses are recommended, but for folate deficiency or risk of recurrent neural tube defect. Interactions: serum phenytoin, phenobarbital and primidone may fall, requiring monitoring and dose adjustment; fluorouracil toxicity may occur and the combination should be avoided; folate supplements enhance lithium efficacy; folate deficiency from methotrexate or trimethoprim cannot be treated with folic acid, folinic acid being required; folic acid may reduce zinc absorption. Undesirable effects: allergic reactions including erythema, rash, pruritus, urticaria, dyspnoea and anaphylactic reaction including shock, rare (1 in 10,000 to 1 in 1000); worsening of co-existing B12 deficiency, frequency not known. Pharmacokinetics: therapeutic folic acid enters the portal circulation largely unchanged, being a poor substrate for dihydrofolate reductase; dietary folates have about half the bioavailability of crystalline folic acid.
